html:
SMTO-TSK-0008 — Select a run

GUID: 40d39954-1c74-44ce-a759-6c6580211659
Slug: run-required
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • You tried to change a setting for one run, but SMTO wasn't told which run you meant. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation that has the run you want to change, then open Agent Checks in the message box controls. Agent Checks only knows which run you mean when it is opened inside that run's conversation.
  2. In the scope list at the top of Agent Checks, choose This run, then make your change again. The This run choice only appears when SMTO knows the run, so picking it sends your change to that run.
  3. If you wanted to change future tasks rather than one run, choose This conversation or Global instead. Those choices don't need a run, so they save without this error.

What success looks like

  • The setting saves and the panel shows it as overridden for this run, with no error under it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If a script or another tool made this change, tell them it needs to include which run to change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run-scoped policy edit (parallel execution, background activities, dependency or resource scheduling, or Context reads) was sent with scope "run" but without a request_id.

What this means

  • A run-scoped policy edit omits its required request identifier. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A run-scoped policy edit omits its required request identifier.

How to diagnose it

  • Check scope and request_id together before changing run-specific settings.

How to fix it

  • Send the run's request_id with every scope "run" PUT to the policy endpoints (for example /api/agent/parallel-execution, /api/agent/background-activities or /api/agent/context-read-policy), or use scope "conversation" or "global" to change future work. In the browser, the This run scope is only offered when the Agent Checks panel has a current request for the open conversation, so this usually comes from a script or an outdated page.
  • Open the intended saved run and its current controls before changing run-scoped settings.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The edit identifies the intended retained run and passes its current state/revision checks.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
